ownership_reason: formatPeriod(long,long,String,boolean,TimeZone) takes per-field differences of the two calendars and, under its own comment 'each initial estimate is adjusted in case it is under 0', normalises a negative field by borrowing from the next larger one (seconds, minutes and hours by while-loops, days and months further down); the millisecond difference is the only field left unadjusted. For the trigger (10:15:30.750 -> 10:16:05.250, 34500 ms) it therefore hands format() seconds=35 and milliseconds=-500. format() only renders the field values it receives: its seconds-then-millis branch (add 1000, left-pad, drop the leading digit) is correct for every normalised value 0..999, which is what formatDuration's remainder arithmetic always supplies and what the passing testFormatDurationHMS / testFormatDurationISO / testFormatPeriodISO pin ('0:00:00.001', '0:00:13.465', '...12.001S'). The wrong seconds digit (35 instead of 34) is appended before the S token is reached, so no edit inside format()'s millisecond branch can repair the output, and lexx tokenises 'H:mm:ss.SSS' correctly (testLexx). The minimal repair restores the millisecond borrow (milliseconds += 1000; seconds -= 1) in formatPeriod.
